title: CMake + wsutil: Use cpuinfo for CPU and CPU feature detection
description:
cpuinfo is a BSD 2-clause licensed library that grew out of
the PyTorch project and is actively developed. It has a
package available in vcpkg, and packages in Linux distributions
including Fedora, openSUSE, Debian, and Ubuntu. It also supports
FreeBSD. It supports x86, x86-64, ARM, and ARM64, and hopefully
should fix the problem of ARM64 friendly string names on Linux.

I tried it with a local build on Windows as well; compiling in
the static library (it is only static on Windows) added 27KB
to dumpcap (284,672 -> 311,808 bytes) in the RelWithDebInfo
configuration.

https://github.com/pytorch/cpuinfo

Fix #20668

AI-Assisted: no

notes.body: mentioned in issue #20668
Thanks. I'm not 100% sure it's necessary from looking at the source code, because it uses `pthread_once` and so forth, but this is for safety.

What about !RPM based systems? Is that considered a followup task?
I'm thinking: - The other setup scripts - Packaging files - (how) does macOS fit in here? - Development containers

The other setup scripts aren't done yet, but could be added. It's available for Debian based distributions and probably others. I didn't add it to the Debian setup script mostly because I'm less familiar with the packaging.

For RPM packaging, there was little to do because it's a shared library. For Windows packaging, if we provided it, it's a static only library so there would be no changes.

It supports macOS. We could package it if we wanted, just as we could package the vcpkg implementation for Windows. I'm not sure that we necessarily need to in either case, because we have working platform specific implementations, but it might be easier than maintaining those.

For the Development containers, after adding to the setup scripts the Development containers can be rebuilt to pick them up.

> It supports macOS.

Which probably isn't too hard, as it presumably pulls all the relevant information from `sysctl()`, as we do.

What it *doesn't* support are NetBSD, OpenBSD, and DragonFly BSD, which our code does support.

Do we use this to fetch some or all of the cache structure and the individual CPU features, or do we just get a friendly name (or, for Arm, at least a less *un*friendly name)?

Perhaps we should submit upstream changes to cpuinfo with our additional platform support.

> > What about !RPM based systems?
> 
> It's available for Debian based distributions and probably others. I didn't add it to the Debian setup script mostly because I'm less familiar with the packaging.

You apparently added it later, although you have to specify `--install-optional`.

...and we continue to use our code if the cpuinfo library either isn't used or doesn't tell us anything, so presumably there won't be any regressions on other platforms.
Making it an optional library in debian-setup.sh means that you have to ask for the optional libraries if you want programs not to leave the CPU entry blank on Arm systems.

Is there any way to get libcpuinfo to *quietly* fail and just tell us "sorry, Dave, I can't do that", so we can try to get the information ourselves?

(I think I 1) looked at the code in the Linux kernel that handles /proc/cpuinfo on System/3x0 (x = 100 for z/Architecture :-)) and 2) possibly printed out /proc/cpuinfo on my "QEMU simulating a z/Architecture workstation while running on Linux in a VM on my Mac" machine, but I don't remember what I found. I'll see if I can dig it up.)

> Is there any way to get libcpuinfo to quietly fail and just tell us "sorry, Dave, I can't do that", so we can try to get the information ourselves?

Their logging is handled through a `clog` library; it has appropriate knobs but unfortunately they seem to be compile time options, and the Debian package is built with the default logging options, instead of not logging to stdio/stderr.

Ubuntu and Debian build the dev package for architectures that cpuinfo doesn't run on. :shrug:

In the short term, the easiest thing might be to not install/depend on libcpuinfo-dev on those architectures until it is supported.

Slightly longer term would be to ask Debian to compile without having the library print to stdout. Even better would be fixing it upstream.
!25136 is a workaround. We don't have a way to specify only certain architectures in debian-setup.py; that might be useful there too.

See also: https://bugs.debian.org/cgi-bin/bugreport.cgi?bug=918177
https://github.com/pytorch/cpuinfo/issues/19

Debian did change the default level to a quieter one, "warning," but it still prints on completely unsupported architectures. IMO a library, as opposed to a application, should have a way to return its error code and string to the calling executable, and not pollute stdout/stderr. We have run into this before with some other libraries, though. (cf. #12222)

changes_data.diff:
@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+#
+# - Find cpuinfo
+# Find CpuInfo includes and library
+#
+#  Creates an IMPORTED library target CpuInfo::CpuInfo
+#  CpuInfo_FOUND     - True if CpuInfo found.
+#
+# Note that the library is static only on Windows, there is no DLL.
+
+include( FindWSWinLibs )
+FindWSWinLibs( "cpuinfo-.*" "CPUINFO_HINTS" )
+
+if( NOT USE_REPOSITORY)
+  find_package(PkgConfig)
+  pkg_search_module(CPUINFO libcpuinfo)
+endif()
+
+find_path(CPUINFO_INCLUDE_DIR
+  NAMES cpuinfo.h
+  HINTS "${CPUINFO_INCLUDEDIR}" "${CPUINFO_HINTS}/include"
+  /usr/include
+  /usr/local/include
+)
+
+find_library(CPUINFO_LIBRARY
+  NAMES cpuinfo
+  HINTS "${CPUINFO_LIBDIR}" "${CPUINFO_HINTS}/lib"
+  PATHS
+  /usr/lib
+  /usr/local/lib
+)
+
+include(FindPackageHandleStandardArgs)
+find_package_handle_standard_args(CpuInfo
+    REQUIRED_VARS   CPUINFO_LIBRARY CPUINFO_INCLUDE_DIR)
+
+if( CpuInfo_FOUND AND NOT TARGET CpuInfo::CpuInfo)
+  # CpuInfo is static only on Windows - vcpkg says:
+  # "On Windows, we can get a cpuinfo.dll, but it exports no symbols."
+  add_library(CpuInfo::CpuInfo UNKNOWN IMPORTED)
+  set_target_properties(CpuInfo::CpuInfo PROPERTIES
+    INTERFACE_INCLUDE_DIRECTORIES "${CPUINFO_INCLUDE_DIR}"
+    IMPORTED_LOCATION "${CPUINFO_LIBRARY}"
+  )
+endif()
